question.worked_solution:
We replace $p$ with $4$ in the expression and simplify as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{2p} & = \\ \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2\cdot 4} & = \\ \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8} & = \\ \frac{2}{8}+\frac{1}{8} & = \\ \frac{2+1}{8} & = \\ \frac{3}{8} & \end{aligned}
$$
